summary: Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose (hypromellose, HPMC) is a hydrophilic cellulose-ether polymer used as an over-the-counter ophthalmic lubricant / artificial tear (commonly 0.3-0.5%) for the temporary relief of dry, irritated eyes. Instilled on the ocular surface it acts as a demulcent, forming a viscous, water-retaining film that lubricates the eye, increases tear-film stability and prolongs the contact time of moisture with the cornea and conjunctiva. Its action is purely local and physical with negligible systemic absorption, so systemic considerations (pregnancy, lactation, renal/hepatic dosing, drug interactions, overdose) are not applicable. Hypromellose is also one of the most widely used pharmaceutical excipients, serving as a film-coating agent, binder, viscosity enhancer, and sustained-release matrix former in oral tablets.

admin: For use in the eyes only - do not inject or swallow
Wash hands; tilt the head back, pull down the lower lid and instill 1-2 drops into the conjunctival sac
Do not touch the dropper or single-use tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Remove soft contact lenses before use unless the product is specifically labelled as safe with lenses; wait before reinserting
Discard single-use (preservative-free) units immediately after use; do not reuse
If using more than one type of eye drop, separate instillations by at least 5 minutes
Do not use if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy
moa: Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose is a hydrophilic cellulose-ether polymer that acts as an ophthalmic demulcent. When instilled onto the eye it forms a viscous, water-retaining film over the corneal and conjunctival surface. This film lubricates the ocular surface, increases the stability and retention time of the natural tear film, and provides a protective coating that relieves dryness and irritation. The effect is entirely local and physical (a mucomimetic/lubricant action); the polymer has no intrinsic pharmacologic activity and is not significantly absorbed systemically.

pearls: Hydroxypropylmethylcellulose is hypromellose (HPMC), an OTC ocular lubricant / artificial tear for temporary relief of dry, irritated eyes

It is also one of the most common pharmaceutical excipients - used as a tablet film-coating agent, binder, and sustained-release matrix former - so the same name may refer to a coating ingredient rather than an eye drop
Acts as a physical demulcent/lubricant, not a pharmacologic drug; systemic fields are not applicable because absorption is negligible
Preservative-free single-use units are preferred for frequent dosing (more than ~4-6 times daily) or sensitive/post-surgical eyes to avoid preservative toxicity
Persistent dry-eye symptoms beyond 72 hours warrant evaluation for an underlying ocular surface disorder
missed: Not applicable - used as needed for symptom relief rather than on a fixed schedule. Instill a drop whenever dryness or irritation occurs.
overdose: Not applicable - topical ophthalmic lubricant with negligible systemic absorption; overdose is essentially not a concern. Excess drops can be wiped away. If accidentally swallowed, contact a Poison Control Center and manage supportively.
